terms.definition: Stored energy an object has because of its position or shape.
terms.function: Holds energy patiently; converts it into motion when released.
terms.whereItIs: The block resting on the shelf.
terms.whyItMatters: The world's stored power — dams, drawn bows, stretched rubber bands all bank on it.

terms.definition: The height formula: potential energy = mass × gravity × height.
terms.whyItMatters: It makes stored energy measurable and explains why height and mass both fill the store.
terms.whereItIs: The meter readout while the shelf sits.

terms.definition: The vertical distance whose size packs energy into the block.
terms.whyItMatters: Doubling height doubles the stored energy — the measure dam engineers bank on.
terms.whereItIs: The scale guide behind the shelf.

terms.definition: The conversion of stored energy into kinetic (or heat) energy.
terms.whyItMatters: Power delivery — a falling block, a dropping hammer, a rolling coaster is this moment in action.
terms.whereItIs: The instant the block falls after the release button taps.
